title: Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS & Smith et al. (2006) PNAS Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Phyllotaxis Reference Dataset

primary_sources.citation: Jönsson H, Heisler MG, Shapiro BE, Meyerowitz EM, Mjolsness E (2006) An auxin-driven polarized transport model for phyllotaxis. PNAS 103(5):1633-1638
key_equations: da_i/dt = rho_0 - mu * a_i + T * sum_{j in N(i)} (P_ji * a_j - P_ij * a_i) + D * sum_{j in N(i)} (a_j - a_i)
P_ij = P_i * exp(c_1 * a_j) / sum_{k in N(i)} exp(c_1 * a_k)
Linear instability eigenvalue on 1D/2D cellular ring: sigma(k) = -mu + 2 * (T * P_0 * (c_1 * a_0 - 1) - D) * (1 - cos(k * l_0)) - kappa_4 * (1 - cos(k * l_0))^2

primary_sources.citation: Smith RS, Guyomarc'h S, Mandel T, Reinhardt D, Kuhlemeier C, Prusinkiewicz P (2006) A plausible model of phyllotaxis. PNAS 103(5):1301-1306
key_equations: PIN1_i->j = PIN1_i * b^(a_j) / sum_{k in N(i)} b^(a_k)   where c_1 = ln(b)
Primordium initiation threshold a_i >= a_thresh in peripheral zone (r in [R_CZ, R_PZ]), followed by radial tissue advection v_r(r) = gamma_adv * r and vascular sink depletion mu_prim * a_i

primary_sources.citation: Reinhardt D et al. (2003) Regulation of phyllotaxis by polar auxin transport. Nature 426:255-260
key_findings: NPA (1-N-naphthylphthalamic acid) or pin1-1 mutation blocks polar auxin transport (T -> 0), producing a bare pin-formed shoot apex with zero primordia
Localized microapplication of exogenous IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) lanolin paste onto an NPA-treated or pin1 apex induces a single lateral organ primordium at the site of application

primary_sources.citation: Geldner N, Friml J, Stierhof Y-D, Jürgens G, Palme K (2001) Auxin transport inhibitors block PIN1 cycling and vesicle trafficking. Nature 413:425-428
key_findings: PIN1 cycles continuously between the plasma membrane and endosomal compartments; brefeldin A (BFA) blocks exocytosis and internalises plasma-membrane PIN1 into BFA compartments within 1-2 h (reversible on wash-out)
Auxin transport inhibitors (TIBA, NPA at high dose) also interfere with PIN1 vesicle trafficking

primary_sources.citation: Paciorek T, Zažímalová E, Ruthardt N, Petrášek J, Stierhof Y-D, Kleine-Vehn J, Morris DA, Emans N, Jürgens G, Geldner N, Friml J (2005) Auxin inhibits endocytosis and promotes its own efflux from cells. Nature 435:1251-1256
key_findings: Auxin inhibits clathrin-dependent endocytosis of PIN proteins, increasing PIN abundance at the plasma membrane and auxin efflux (a candidate cellular mechanism for up-the-gradient PIN1 polarisation)

primary_sources.citation: Bayer EM, Smith RS, Mandel T, Nakayama N, Sauer M, Prusinkiewicz P, Kuhlemeier C (2009) Integration of transport-based models for phyllotaxis and midvein formation. Genes & Development 23:373-384
key_equations: Epidermal up-the-gradient PIN1 polarisation (Smith/Jönsson 2006) coupled to subepidermal with-the-flux canalization: PIN1 allocation to wall i->j increases with the auxin flux already crossing it, producing a narrow provascular strand from the L1 convergence point to the existing vasculature

primary_sources.citation: Mitchison GJ (1980) A model for vein formation in higher plants. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London B 207:79-109
key_equations: Canalization: wall transport capacity increases with the flux through it (superlinear feedback) so that an initially diffuse flux field collapses into discrete single-file channels

primary_sources.citation: Mitchison GJ (1981) The polar transport of auxin and vein patterns in plants. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 295:461-471
key_findings: Polar auxin transport with flux-dependent carrier allocation reproduces vein strand formation and connection to pre-existing vasculature

primary_sources.citation: Feugier FG, Mochizuki A, Iwasa Y (2005) Self-organization of the vascular system in plant leaves: Inter-dependent dynamics of auxin flux and carrier proteins. Journal of Theoretical Biology 236:366-375
key_equations: dP_ij/dt = alpha * Phi(J_ij) - beta * P_ij with Phi(J) = J^n / (K^n + J^n); discrete strands require superlinear feedback (n > 1) and a limited cellular carrier pool

primary_sources.citation: Scarpella E, Marcos D, Friml J, Berleth T (2006) Control of leaf vascular patterning by polar auxin transport. Genes & Development 20:1015-1027
key_findings: PIN1::PIN1-GFP marks narrow preprocambial strands (1-2 cells wide) in which PIN1 is polarised along the strand axis toward the pre-existing vasculature

phyllotactic_mode_regimes.label: Spiral Fibonacci (137.5°)
phyllotactic_mode_regimes.source: Smith et al. (2006) PNAS Fig. 3 & Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS Fig. 4

phyllotactic_mode_regimes.label: Distichous Alternate (180.0°)
phyllotactic_mode_regimes.source: Smith et al. (2006) PNAS Fig. 4A (reduced central zone / smaller meristem ring)

phyllotactic_mode_regimes.label: Decussate Opposite Pairs (90.0°)
phyllotactic_mode_regimes.source: Smith et al. (2006) PNAS Fig. 4B & Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS Fig. 3

phyllotactic_mode_regimes.label: Tricussate Whorled Triplets (60°/120°)
phyllotactic_mode_regimes.source: Smith et al. (2006) PNAS Fig. 4C (enlarged meristem ring / 3 simultaneous peaks)

wild_type_control.description: Intact up-the-gradient PIN1 polar transport (T = 1.20 h^-1, c_1 = 1.85)

npa_pin1_polar_transport_block.description: 10 uM NPA treatment or pin1-1 loss-of-function mutant (T = 0.0 h^-1, passive diffusion only)
npa_pin1_polar_transport_block.phenotype: Pin-formed bare inflorescence apex lacking lateral organ primordia (Reinhardt et al. 2003 Nature Fig. 1)

exogenous_iaa_microdroplet_rescue.description: NPA/pin1-1 apex + localized 1 mM IAA lanolin microdroplet at phi_paste = 60.0 deg on peripheral ring
exogenous_iaa_microdroplet_rescue.phenotype: Single localized radial organ primordium rescued at exact microapplication site (Reinhardt et al. 2003 Nature Fig. 2; Smith et al. 2006 Fig. 5)

pin1_trafficking_kinetics.description: Explicit PIN1 exocytosis/endocytosis cycling used in Pass 3 (Jönsson et al. 2006 PIN1 cycling; Geldner et al. 2001; Paciorek et al. 2005): dP_ij/dt = k_exo f(a_j) P_cyt_i - k_endo P_ij with P_cyt_i + sum_j P_ij = P_tot
pin1_trafficking_kinetics.targeting_function: f_ij = exp(c_1 (a_j - a_0)) (up-the-gradient exocytosis targeting; QSS reduces to the Boltzmann law as k_endo/(k_exo sum_k f_ik) -> 0)
pin1_trafficking_kinetics.reference_plasma_membrane_fraction_note: Qualitative band edge from Geldner 2001 Fig. 1 / Heisler 2005 (PIN1 predominantly at the plasma membrane in untreated cells); not a published quantitative fraction

subepidermal_canalization.description: Quasi-3D (2D vertical slice) with-the-flux canalization of the provascular strand beneath one L1 primordium (Bayer et al. 2009; Mitchison 1980/1981; Feugier et al. 2005). NOT a full 3D meristem.
subepidermal_canalization.reference_strand_width_source: Scarpella et al. (2006) Genes Dev 20:1015-1027 Figs. 1-3 PIN1::PIN1-GFP preprocambial strands; Bayer et al. (2009) Genes Dev 23:373-384 Figs. 3-5 midvein strand
subepidermal_canalization.reference_delivered_fraction_note: Idealised canalization: all L1 efflux conducted to the pre-existing vasculature (Mitchison 1980)
